findings_and_connected_questions.title: The equipment key can identify only one of multiple displaced items
findings_and_connected_questions.trace: The authored burgonet occupies rigid-armor head and the gorget occupies rigid-armor neck, so the canonical conflict predicate allows them to coexist. The barbute occupies head, face and neck, and conflicts with both. The shared t input addresses all three body locations. For one placement, template inputOccupants collects at most one conflicting occupant per requirement and then chooses only the maximum occupant for that input; the generated keyboard option can therefore carry just one of the two displaced objects. The equipment dialog presents one icon and accessible name for that input, while selection is sent with replace_occupied=true. The authoritative reducer independently collects every conflicting root into a set, validates displaced items and removes every accepted conflict. The older full placement label computes multiple conflicts, but this inspected dialog uses structured inputOccupants and does not present that complete label or a replacement-set confirmation.
findings_and_connected_questions.conditions: Requires both appropriate pieces already equipped without protected children, a compatible authorized current actor and the submitted replacement succeeding; assumes stored catalog projection matches the authored definitions. No current player state, loss, browser rendering, actual click or successful reducer operation was observed. Equipment remains in inventory rather than being destroyed; no claim of irreversible loss. Whether the interface must explicitly show/confirm the entire set is a product-legibility decision; a single icon cannot represent both distinct identities.
findings_and_connected_questions.future_repair_direction: Derive the complete preview of the authoritative displacement set for the selected placement and present the affected items before a replacement is committed, coordinated with current graph freshness, attachment capacity, child constraints and server authority. Avoid transferring UI preview into authority; preserve legitimate multi-slot atomic replacement.

findings_and_connected_questions.title: Parent and occupant u64 identities are serialized as JavaScript numbers
findings_and_connected_questions.trace: Inventory item IDs are auto-increment u64 primary keys. The template inserts parentInventoryItemId and occupant inventoryItemId as JSON numeric values. JavaScript parses them as Number, sorts parent IDs by numeric subtraction, and serializes selected parent IDs into attachment_targets; the server decodes that field as u64. An ID above 2^53 can lose integer precision in this path, and two distinct valid u64 values may become the same Number. The root moving item is independently sent from an HTML data attribute as a string.
findings_and_connected_questions.conditions: Requires an inventory ID outside the exact Number integer range and an affected attachment or display path; no such actual database value, collision, wrong parent or successful operation was observed. Server still validates parent ownership, compatible point and tags, required location and cycle, so no authorization bypass follows. No runtime probe or fabricated fixture was used.
findings_and_connected_questions.future_repair_direction: Preserve exact identity at JSON/native boundaries, such as canonical decimal strings with checked server admission and coordinated comparison; validate all producers/consumers and tie-breaking without a compatibility shim. The authoritative schema remains the identity owner.

findings_and_connected_questions.classification: conditional open policy/consistency question, no established false-fit defect
findings_and_connected_questions.trace: The UI reconstructs an occupied fit_zone from the compiled core catalog using item name, placement ID and requirement index; a missing lookup becomes None. The core conflict rule treats None as whole-location reservation, so this fallback is conservative for otherwise matching location/channel/order. The reducer calculates conflicts from persisted item placement definitions, and init projects authored definitions into the database.
findings_and_connected_questions.conditions: A compiled web catalog and persisted database catalog may be synchronized; no catalog skew, missing graph row or false conflict has been observed. A missing UI graph entry and a legitimate whole-location None are distinct facts despite shared value. Current catalog versioning/update/deployment policy remains open.
findings_and_connected_questions.future_repair_direction: Establish catalog identity and synchronized projection contract, and distinguish unavailable lookup from authored whole-location value if mismatch is possible; keep exact typed fit rules and authoritative current reducer validation.
relationships: 059 q1749 explicitly left fit_zone None semantics pending; this read establishes that None conflicts with all zones in same location/channel/order, while catalog-coherence/authority remains pending. 059 q1557 names a broader canonical placement identity/fit owner question, not automatically this same first cut.

nonfindings.text: Attachment helper matches channel and order, optional reached body location, tags with explicit empty wildcard, and rejects self/descendant parents. Backend repeats ownership, location, tags, cycle and capacity validation; capacity-zero options may support replacement and are not automatically bad.
fit_zone None represents whole location, so a missing fit lookup is not a permissive no-conflict value under the inspected canonical rule. Static-versus-persisted catalog consistency remains open.

Encumbrance meter displays the existing EncumbranceSummary.penalty_fraction, and source assertions describe clamping; a display label alone establishes no separate fatigue, movement or combat penalty.

Quality values passed through these two visible paths are clamped 1–5 before the match; direct internal callers outside these inspected paths would require separate proof before any unreachable panic claim.

Standard authored catalog projection sets base_value to Some; shared inventory item_value renders a dash for missing value, while the earlier quest report describes a different fallback. A missing/failed catalog remains conditional, not proof that a valid current authored item lacks a price.
The self/descendant search uses a visited set and the roots walk a path set to stop cycles. This is not proof the whole external graph is valid or bounded.
All existing tests and source fixtures were inspected only as text, with no test or product execution.

Can live inventory IDs reach or be externally imported above 2^53, and which other JSON/DOM APIs carry them as numbers?
Are compiled web and persisted strategic catalog versions required to agree, and how are stale placement IDs, requirement indices and missing rows exposed?
Can current authored attachment requirements create greedy allocation failure despite a feasible alternative, and are full target slots selected for replacement intentionally?

How should q513–516 graph observation failures, q548 native IDs, q1749 fit/attachment, q1557 catalog identity, and prior encumbrance-completeness finding be linked without conflating distinct first cuts?
